cap: NPD master flow: the five phases with their procedure codes, the five gates beneath them, and the rework and action closure return.
Phase 1 — Pre-Assessment, and the Gate-1 decision with its three outcomes.
Phase 2 — Definition and Planning. The Design History File is opened here and maintained through every later phase.
Gate-2 — Plan Approval, and what happens on each outcome.
Phase 3A — concept, system and detail design, with the design review loop that spans all three.
Phase 3B — process design through to the intermediate project review.
Gate-3 — Design Approval, and what happens on each outcome.
Phase 4A — production preparation. Every rework loop in this phase returns through NPDP4010 ECO Release.
Phase 4B — verification and validation. Both procedures found faults that were invisible in the local environment.
Gate-4 — Production Approval, and what happens on each outcome.
Phase 5 — Launch and Post-Production. Gate-5 approves readiness before NPDP5040 launch, not after it.
How to read any of the flows: applicability, the acceptance test, progress or rework, and what each gate decides.
